Key Research Thinking Patterns: Ecological Momentary Assessment of Dynamic Processes: Utilizing high-frequency longitudinal designs to capture real-time fluctuations in affect and behavior, specifically employing 10-day Experience Sampling Method (ESM) and daily diary protocols to map temporal dynamics of job boredom and counterproductive work behavior.

Experimental Causal Inference via RCTs: Implementing randomized controlled trials with between-person intervention grouping and within-person strategy comparison to test the efficacy of cognitive reappraisal modules in mitigating negative workplace outcomes and enhancing job performance.

Multilevel Latent Change Modeling: Applying Latent Change Score (LCS) modeling and cross-lagged coupling analysis to disentangle reciprocal causality and temporal precedence between psychological states (e.g., boredom) and behavioral outcomes (e.g., CWB) over time.

Psychometric Rigor and Scale Validation: Conducting comprehensive psychometric validation procedures, including item generation, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and multi-sample validation, to ensure the reliability of novel constructs such as attitudes towards AI application and perceived overqualification.
Summary Description: JeongJin Kim specializes in organizational psychology, focusing on the dynamic interplay between employee well-being, workplace behavior, and technology adoption. By integrating psychometric scale development with rigorous multilevel modeling, Kim investigates how daily affective fluctuations drive outcomes like burnout and counterproductive work behavior. His methodology uniquely combines high-frequency ecological momentary assessments (ESM) with randomized controlled trials to test interventions, such as cognitive reappraisal, in naturalistic work settings. This approach bridges the gap between theoretical models of effort-recovery and practical HR strategies, offering evidence-based solutions for managing overqualified talent, mitigating job insecurity related to AI, and optimizing organizational health through targeted emotional regulation.
